speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bullous Pemphigoid.

The skin biopsy showing acantholysis and intraepidermal blistering, combined with your painful mucosal ulcers and recent history of hiking/exposure to potential allergens, points towards an autoimmune blistering disorder rather than a drug eruption like captopril-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome. While the negative anti-Histidyl-Lysine antibodies help rule out pemphigus vulgaris, the specific histopathology confirms a diagnosis of bullous pemphigoid, which often presents with tense bullae and can involve mucous membranes. I recommend continuing with supportive care and potentially starting topical or systemic corticosteroids.
